extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting articles to arXiv (researchers, academics, preprint authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting articles to the arXiv repository, covering accepted file formats, figures, filenames, metadata, versioning, and announcement scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information. To submit an article, use the Submit form or select 'START NEW SUBMISSION' from your user page.

rubrics_metrics.name: License or certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission you must either grant arXiv the stated license or certify an alternate license that conveys equivalent distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv prefers TeX/LaTeX because it is an open format that does not hide information. Users of word processors such as Microsoft Word should save documents as PDF and submit that. Scanned documents are not accepted. Note: the page also states they will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source for certain reasons—follow the detailed format guidance on arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG, GIF, PNG, and PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PS/EPS for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photographic images, GIF/PNG for non-photographic bitmaps. PDF figures are only acceptable when using PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures, tables, sections or submit abstract-only
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. 'Abstract only' submissions are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value. Ensure the full article (including figures/tables/sections) is included in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage figure file sizes for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will be unable to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your submission has a large figure, include it but make all possible efforts to reduce its size. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators. Remember many arXiv users have poor network connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include figures with LaTeX source using standard macros
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues, so seek help from colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on the arXiv system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that internal file references such as LaTeX figure inclusion commands match case exactly (e.g., Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited support for data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for details on how to provide such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate title/abstract information must be prepared; this metadata is used on abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions on preparation of title/abstract information to ensure proper display and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before finalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them or contact arXiv administrators if problems cannot be resolved. Use the Unsubmit icon on your user page to return the submission to incomplete status if you need to modify before public announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit and resubmission behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, select the Unsubmit icon to return it to incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting takes the article out of the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing rules and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits and final submission before 14:00 US Eastern Time (Monday–Friday) will not delay announcement. arXiv encourages updates and corrections, but replacement rules apply (see next item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace rather than create new submission for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacing the original preserves the record and avoids duplicate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility and third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged as they often cause problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because putting articles on arXiv entails responsibilities, authors should submit themselves to avoid mistakes caused by lack of self-interest or related factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required additional information: affiliations and report numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is also required for submission: institutional affiliation for the author(s) and official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate institutional affiliations and any official report numbers when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and announcement scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are normally made public Sunday through Thursday, with no announcements Friday or Saturday. There is a schedule mapping submission receipt windows (US Eastern times) to announcement times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the current time at the arXiv main site and the 'freeze' time before submission; announcements depend on the submission time window (detailed schedule shown). Note policy change 2017-01 regarding announcement order and effect of edits.
